text: Fixed in middleware/proxy.go. With no targets, both balancers panicked instead of failing gracefully: `randomBalancer.Next` called `rand.Intn(0)` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` did `b.i % uint32(0)` (division by zero). Now each `Next` returns nil when the target list is empty, and `ProxyWithConfig` checks the result and returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (HTTP 503) instead of dereferencing a nil target. Verified with a temporary test (round-robin, random, and remove-all-targets cases all return 503, no panic) and the full existing suite still passes (`go test ./...` ok, `go vet` clean).

`MethodOverride()` returns an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` — specifically `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)`, i.e. the MethodOverride middleware built with the default config (`Skipper: DefaultSkipper`, `Getter: MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)`). The returned middleware only rewrites the request method when the original method is `POST` and the getter returns a non-empty value, then calls `next(c)`.
Already fixed and verified (middleware/proxy.go: empty-target balancers now return nil and ProxyWithConfig returns 503 instead of panicking).

Still working on the router.go bug (#4). I've narrowed it to the router's Find/route-registration handling of paths that have no routable content (e.g. a route registered with an empty/whitespace-only or otherwise non-matching path), and I'm reproducing it against the existing router tests now. ETA ~10 minutes.
`DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` (middleware/decompress.go:76-78), i.e. `DefaultSkipper` — the function that always returns false, so no request is skipped.

It panics: `BodyLimitWithConfig` calls `bytes.Parse(config.Limit)` and on error does `panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))` (middleware/body_limit.go:63-66). Otherwise it stores the parsed byte count in `config.limit` and builds the limited-reader pool.

`BodyDumpWithConfig` panics: `if config.Handler == nil { panic("echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function") }` (middleware/body_dump.go:55-57). Otherwise it defaults `Skipper` to `DefaultBodyDumpConfig.Skipper` and returns the middleware that buffers request/response bodies and calls `config.Handler(c, reqBody, resBody.Bytes())`.
`DefaultRedirectConfig.Code` is `http.StatusMovedPermanently` (301) — middleware/redirect.go:26-30. (When a user-supplied config has `Code == 0`, the middleware substitutes this default.)

Done: empty responses no longer leak a 10-byte gzip header into the body. `gzipResponseWriter.Write` now returns early for zero-length writes, so an empty body stays empty (and no bogus Content-Type is sniffed) while Content-Encoding is dropped for empty responses. Full suite still green.

Done: map binding now supports map[string][]string. `bindData` delegates map destinations to a new `bindDataToMap`, which binds the whole []string slice when the map element type is a slice and the first value otherwise (map[string]string / map[string]interface{} behaviour unchanged). Verified: map[string][]string{"foo":{"bar","baz"}} binds correctly, no panic; full suite green.

Done: `context.Scheme()` now only honours valid scheme values — X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme are used only when they are exactly "http" or "https" (X-Forwarded-Ssl only when "on"), otherwise it falls back to "http". Invalid headers are ignored as the doc contract (returns "http" or "https") requires.

Done: `ProxyWithConfig` now returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of panicking when the balancer has no targets; both `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` return nil for an empty target list (previously rand.Intn(0) / modulo-by-zero panics).

Not fixed yet. I've fuzzed router.Add/Find over many route/path combinations (including paths with no routable content) without reproducing a panic, so the divergence is narrower than a crash — I'm now checking the Find/NotFound handling for paths that match no route node (and the "" / "/*" registration paths). ETA ~8 min.

Not fixed yet. The suspicious area is route registration for two groups sharing the same path: `Echo.add` keys routes by `method+path` in `e.router.routes`, and `Group.Use` registers `""`/`/*` catch-alls, so a second group on the same path can overwrite the first group's route/middleware entry. Verifying that against the group middleware tests now. ETA ~8 min.
